title: Zohar Symbols: a computed dictionary of the Zohar's kinnuyim
description:
Zohar Symbols is an open-access, bilingual (English/Spanish) computed dictionary of the symbols (kinnuyim) of the Zohar, for curious readers, live at zohar.digital. The Zohar speaks in images (the moon, the river, the bride, gold, the beard), and each image points to a sefirah. Deterministic code reads the Aramaic text of Sefer ha-Zohar, finds every image, counts where it appears and what it appears with, and shows the passages.

Corpus. The main body of the Zohar (three volumes, Mantua pagination) from Hebrew Wikisource, CC BY-SA 4.0, fetched from 29 pinned page revisions: 1,630 folio-sides, 15,909 passages, 832,463 tokens, in nine text streams (main, Ra'aya Meheimna, Midrash ha-Ne'lam, Sitrei Torah, Raza de-Razin, Tosefta, Matnitin, other, addendum) and eleven strata including Idra Rabba and Idra Zuta.

Method. Tokens are lemmatised with aramaic_core from the Aramaic Root Atlas plus Zohar-specific overrides; 139 seeded symbols (Cordovero, Pardes Rimonim gate 23; Gikatilla, Sha'arei Orah; Zohar usage) are tagged by surface and root aliases (54,003 mentions); co-occurrence and PMI over passages (5,825 pairs), symbol states, strata distributions and surfaced passages are computed. The rebuilt tables are checked against a committed sha256 at every deploy. No model produces any number.

Translations. 678 surfaced passages are translated into English and Spanish (1,356 texts) by Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), attributed on the page, not reviewed by specialists, each stored with model id, prompt version and source hash.

Interpretations. Under 677 of those translations, a short plain-language reading, "What this passage means", in English and Spanish, by the same model, labelled as inferred: not a traditional commentary, not reviewed by specialists. The method is written up in docs/METHOD.md.

Licence. Code MIT; text, tables and translations CC BY-SA 4.0, attributing Hebrew Wikisource. Source: github.com/Jossifresben/zohar-symbols.

The concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23305097 always resolves to the latest version.
